rationale: Although this qualitative ethnographic case study is empirical (c3 = yes) and mentions sanitation workers in Dhaka, its topic is occupational stigma, hereditary cleaning labour ("dirty work"), workplace harassment, institutional distance from general social-protection schemes, and constrained worker agency among Harijan municipal sweepers. It does not examine household or community access to water or sanitation services (c1 = no), legal/administrative mechanisms governing water or sanitation service access (c2 = no), or any water/sanitation service-access outcome (c4 = no). Excluded under E01 (wrong topic).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both the narrow rule-type reading and the plain wording of Criterion 2 because the study is an occupational/caste ethnography of sanitation workers' labour stigma, social-protection distance, and worker agency rather than household or community water or sanitation service access (failing Criteria 1 and 4, as well as Criterion 2 with respect to service-access governance).

evidence_quotes.quote: Social Exclusion, Occupational Stigma, and Constrained Agency among Harijan Sanitation Workers in Urban Bangladesh

caste-inflected occupational stigma that surrounds their labour, together with gendered constraints on mobility and settlement-based exclusion, may narrow the extent to which paid work is translated into meaningful agency.
showing how caste, gender and space jointly produce constrained agency even under conditions of formal wage employment.
